datasets.DATA-01: SIGCOMM'22 'Vivisecting Mobility Management in 5G Cellular Networks' artifact, github.com/SIGCOMM22-5GMobility/artifact @ c612c6fe (2022-06-26); U.S. commercial networks (Verizon/T-Mobile/AT&T), Minneapolis-area drives; Git-LFS files D1/D2 not fetched
datasets.DATA-02: UCC MISL 'Beyond Throughput, the Next Generation: a 5G Dataset with Channel and Context Metrics' (MMSys'20), github.com/uccmisl/5Gdataset @ 306d92eb (2020-06-19); one Irish operator, Cork, static + car, 83 one-second traces

A_handover_duration.definition: T1 = 'MR' column (s); T2 = 'HO'+'RCH' columns (s), as in the artifact's figure-9 script; 'FULL' equals HO+RCH (max |diff| = 379 s)

cross_check_MOB-02e.paper_quote: average HO duration NSA 167 ms, LTE 76 ms, SA 110 ms (Hassan et al. §5.2)
cross_check_MOB-02e.verdict: NOT REPRODUCED by simple statistics of the released file: the SA median (110 ms) matches the quoted SA figure, LTE/NSA do not under any of the subsets tried (all types, PCell/MCG only, T1 <= 1 s). The file has missing RCH in 11,101 rows and missing MR in 3,919, and T1 is heavy-tailed (NSA mean 303 ms vs median 65 ms; 4.9 % of NSA events have T1 > 1 s). The authors' filtering is not in the artifact. Consequence for the paper: quote MOB-02e only as the authors' stated averages; for any figure or per-budget share, use the released per-event distribution and say so.

B_handover_spacing.note: distance between consecutive handovers in metres as released for the paper's Fig. 11 ('distance_ho'); '_ideal_' files are distances between PCI changes ('distance_pci'). HO/km = 1000/mean spacing; HO/h = HO/km x speed.
B_handover_spacing.cross_check_MOB-02c: paper: mmWave HO every 0.13 km, mid-band 0.35 km, low-band 0.4 km; distance.json: MID_BAND_LTE_HO=559 m, LOW_BAND_SCG_ADD=405 m, LOW_BAND_SCG_MOD=415 m, LOW_BAND_SCG_REL=428 m, MMWAVE_SCG_ADD=128 m, MMWAVE_SCG_MOD=118 m, MMWAVE_SCG_REL=142 m

C_handover_rate_from_gps_trace.note: PCI-change counts are an independent re-derivation from the released 1-s trace, not the authors' number; runs with < 0.5 km of GPS travel (HOME) get no per-km rate. handoffType is the 5G-Tracker app's own event code (0 = none).

D_tcp_rtt_nsa_modes.time_unit_note: time_since_start advances in steps of 100 (ms assumed: 10 samples/s); SS_RTT_AVG is the kernel's smoothed RTT (ms) as reported by `ss`

E_5g_nsa_pdsch_throughput_driving.note: PDSCH = NR-leg downlink PHY throughput under a saturating iperf download while driving (Verizon, mmWave/low-band NSA loop); this is the direction that carries the server's Certificate + signature flight, the largest flight of a PQ handshake

C0_classical.note: bytes x 8 / measured PDSCH Mbps, per sample; lower bound (no scheduling delay, no retransmission). The p99/max tail comes from samples at a few kbit/s (outage or idle scheduler moments), i.e. a handshake started there stalls rather than 'takes 3 min'

C1_hybrid_kex.note: bytes x 8 / measured PDSCH Mbps, per sample; lower bound (no scheduling delay, no retransmission). The p99/max tail comes from samples at a few kbit/s (outage or idle scheduler moments), i.e. a handshake started there stalls rather than 'takes 3 min'

C2_full_pq.note: bytes x 8 / measured PDSCH Mbps, per sample; lower bound (no scheduling delay, no retransmission). The p99/max tail comes from samples at a few kbit/s (outage or idle scheduler moments), i.e. a handshake started there stalls rather than 'takes 3 min'

F_video_conf_driving.note: Application-reported one-way latency of a laptop video call tethered to a 5G phone while driving (artifact's Fig. 4); the relevant clinical analogue is the ambulance video/telemetry stream, not surgery

download_Driving_dl_kbps_active_seconds.note: file-download traces, seconds with DL_bitrate > 0 (application-layer rate; the only traffic class here that is not rate-limited by a player)

download_Static_dl_kbps_active_seconds.note: file-download traces, seconds with DL_bitrate > 0 (application-layer rate; the only traffic class here that is not rate-limited by a player)

Driving_ping_avg_ms.note: PINGAVG column where numeric (ICMP to a fixed host, per the dataset README)

Driving_cell_changes_per_km_over_traces.note: RAWCELLID changes per speed-integrated km, one value per driving trace

Driving_totals.note: GPS fixes repeat for 10-15 rows and several fixes share a 1-s timestamp, so the GPS path length under-counts; the speed-integrated figure is used for per-km rates

Static_ping_avg_ms.note: PINGAVG column where numeric (ICMP to a fixed host, per the dataset README)

C0_classical.note: bytes x 8 / per-second application DL rate, driving file-download seconds; lower bound

C1_hybrid_kex.note: bytes x 8 / per-second application DL rate, driving file-download seconds; lower bound

C2_full_pq.note: bytes x 8 / per-second application DL rate, driving file-download seconds; lower bound

DATA-01 (SIGCOMM'22): Section IV: distribution (not just the mean) of handover interruption T2 for LTE/NSA/SA, 43,856 events -> the user-plane outage a clinical stream sees per handover, and the share exceeding the 2/20/100 ms budgets
Section IV: HO spacing distributions on freeway drives (Fig. 11 files) -> HO/km and HO/h at speed as a distribution; distance.json reproduces MOB-02c (0.13/0.35/0.4 km)
Section IV/V: RTT time series around handover events (Fig. 7 file) -> RTT anchor measured, not assumed

Section V: measured NSA downlink PHY throughput while driving (Fig. 12 file) -> airtime of C0/C1/C2 as a distribution; Section VII: a video call under mobility with handoff timestamps (Fig. 4 files) as the ambulance-stream analogue
DATA-02 (UCC Irish 5G): Section V: per-second application DL rate under driving with cell id, RSRP/SNR/CQI and ICMP RTT -> a second operator/country for the airtime distribution and a cell-change rate per km in a city (Cork) rather than a freeway

caveats_to_state: Both are downlink-centric consumer measurements (phones/laptops), U.S. and Irish networks, 2019-2022; no NB-IoT, LTE-M, BLE or 802.15.6 traces -> the constrained-link rows of Table II stay nominal unless a third dataset is added
Application-layer DL rates (DATA-02) and PHY PDSCH (DATA-01) are not the same quantity; airtime from either is a lower bound
DATA-01 has no stated license in the repository; DATA-02 is GPL-3.0 (fine to analyse and cite; ask before bundling as SM)
